columns.text:
Welcome to my practice. 

I am a qualified psychodynamic therapist working in Edinburgh and online. 

I offer a reflective, consistent space to explore your thoughts, feelings and difficult experiences. You might come with a specific concern, or with longstanding struggles in your relationships, your sense of self, or more existential challenges. We will move at your pace and listen closely to you. 

I encourage you to read a bit [about me](/about) and [my approach](/approach) to psychotherapy. If something about this website resonates, I’d love to hear from you.

# *It’s a joy to be hidden and a disaster not to be found.*

D. W. Winnicott (Playing and Reality, 1971)

You do **not** need to be able to clearly articulate what is wrong in order to seek help. You may come in because you have a vague sense of unease, worry or feel that something does not feel quite right. 

These are some of the difficulties people bring to me:

items.question: Emotional Difficulties
items.answer:
Anxiety, stress, dread or panic 

Depression, exhaustion or low-mood

Feelings of shame, disgust, cringe or embarrassment 

Aggression and anger management

Feminist rage

items.question: Interpersonal Concerns
items.answer:
Relationship difficulties with partner, parents, friends or siblings

Effects of trauma, abuse or sexual violence

Difficulties in childhood or adolescence

items.question: Grief and Change
items.answer:
Loss of a loved person, group, or a part of your identity 

Life transitions

items.question: Self-Exploration
items.answer:
Understand yourself better

Body image and gender identity

Impact of culture, race and systemic oppression

items.question: Existential Concerns
items.answer:
Isolation, emptiness and loneliness

Struggles with finding meaning, fulfilment or purpose

columns.text:
# *It’s a joy to be hidden and a disaster not to be found.*

D. W. Winnicott (Playing and Reality, 1971)

My primary aim is to build a therapeutic relationship in which you are able to be your most genuine self. In this relationship, the client is the expert, not the therapist. You will not find me imposing behavioural changes or offering pastoral advice. Although, I do often draw our attention to interpersonal dynamics in the past and present. I listen to understand you as a whole: your relationships, your cultural context and your childhood. We collaboratively develop insights and new possibilities of relating to yourself.

  

No therapeutic dialogue is complete without acknowledging the influence of sociocultural context on our health, wellbeing and identities. I am always interested in your experiences with your culture, gender, religion, environment/climate, political conditions and beyond. I also welcome your disagreements and challenges to my thinking. 

  

I adhere closely to the ethical guidelines laid out by BACP. My clinical work is supported by regular supervision.

For a long time, I imagined the psychodynamic therapist as a cold, humourless (and sexist!) man who analyses you while you lie on a couch. This stereotype broke during my training. Psychoanalysis has evolved so much since the time of Freud! Today it is about so much else than strict interpretation and analysis. 

  

Many people come to therapy because they are anxious, depressed or self-critical. However, on examining things further, it becomes clear that their relationships feel strained or lacking. Psychodynamic therapy places importance on your relationships: to yourself, to your friends and partners, to your past, and to me. 

  

Instead of focusing solely on finding solutions or reducing symptoms, it aims to understand a person as a whole, including emotional and relational experiences that are not always fully conscious of. Over time, clients find that they are able to develop relationships that feel more valuable, richer, and less intimidating. They are able to be themselves with others and are more open to navigating conflict. Research shows that this leads to a lasting reduction in their mental health symptoms as well.

Typically, I meet with clients once a week for a 50-minute session.

  

Therapy unfolds through a secure relationship in which there is time to think, to feel, to question, and sometimes simply not to know. There is no set agenda. We begin with whatever feels most relevant for you that week. 

  

We may speak about your memories, beliefs, feelings, dreams, and relationships. Eventually we become curious about patterns and contradictions that usually go unnoticed. The hope is for you to emerge with a greater sense of acceptance, freedom, meaning and joy. 

  

If you’ve made it this far and are feeling encouraged, then it’s likely we can work together. You can reach out to me [here](/contact).

Hi! I’m Rhea. 

I am a reflective, empathetic and passionate practitioner. I hold a COSCA qualification and a BACP membership. I currently practice in-person in Edinburgh and online. 

I began my career as a volunteer counsellor at Hope Park Counselling in Edinburgh. Since, I have had the opportunity to do meaningful, long-term work with adults experiencing a range of emotional and relationship difficulties. 

I believe that psychotherapy is one of the most fascinating and valuable things we can do for ourselves. It offers a rare chance for us to cut through the noise and turn our attention inward. As a therapist, my hope is to offer a warm, unhurried space where you can slow down and listen to all parts of yourself, especially those that feel stuck, hurt or silenced. If you are noticing patterns that don’t seem to change, find yourself avoiding thinking about certain things, or can’t help but feel a certain way, therapy can help you explore this in a safe and gentle way. 

I am trained in the dialogue between the person-centred and psychodynamic theoretical orientations. In simple words, this means that I believe that our relationship is central to therapy. You can read more about my approach here. 

More broadly, I enjoy reading fiction and watching films. Stories, metaphors, dreams and myths are valuable sources of knowledge and are welcome in our work together. I speak English and Hindi/Urdu.

## Qualifications

### 

Master of Counselling (Interpersonal Dialogue), University of Edinburgh, Scotland

Postgraduate Diploma in Advanced Studies and Research in Psychology, Ashoka University, India

Bachelor of Science (Hons.) in Psychology, Ashoka University, India

## Additional Training

January training, group training

## Additional Engagements

My research revolves around the lived experience of menstrual disorders (eg. PMOS/PCOS). I am interested in how patriarchal narratives, gender norms and medicalisation inform one’s relationship to their body, illness and identity. I welcome therapeutic work with individuals impacted by health-related anxieties, chronic pain and body-related concerns.

### Contact Me

If you’d like to explore counselling with me, please fill out this form or write to me at [rhea.psychotherapy@gmail.com](mailto:rhea.psychotherapy@gmail.com). I will respond within 2-3 working days to arrange an initial conversation. 

  

### Initial Consultation 

For therapy to be useful, the client and therapist need to be a good enough fit. To help you get a feel for what it’s like to speak with me, I offer a free consultation (online, 20-30 minutes). I will ask you a few questions about what brings you to my website, and respond to your questions as well. This first call carries no obligation to begin therapy immediately or at all. 

  

### Fee

I charge £55-70 per session, depending on what you can afford. I also offer concession spots to those who may need it.

  

### Locations

I rent rooms in Edinburgh’s Old Town, Newington and Leith. I also work online when necessary. 

  

### Accessibility

My office in Leith is fully accessible to wheelchair users. Please let me know about any other accessibility requirements I should be aware of.

columns.heading: FAQs
columns.subheading: Here are my answers to some questions I am often asked about my practice.

items.question: How many sessions will I need?
items.answer: As many as you feel you need! I suggest we have at least 4 sessions for you to get a good sense of our working relationship. After that, we can decide a number of sessions together or keep our contract open-ended.

items.question: Will you provide a diagnosis?
items.answer: No. I am neither trained to do that nor do I particularly want to reduce the complexity and diversity of the human condition to a medical-psychological category. That said, I understand that labels can provide relief, empowerment, community and even become an opening to greater self-understanding. I am interested in exploring your relationship with the diagnostic labels you bring to the room.

items.question: How does confidentiality work?
items.answer:
**Everything you share with me is confidential**. I have a supervisor with whom I discuss clinical material, but this happens in a confidential, professional and boundaried space. 

I will **<u>never</u>** share any part of our work on any social media platforms. Not even after we have ended our work. My clients’ stories and struggles are not content. I take privacy seriously and intend to protect the sanctity of the therapist-client relationship. I do not have a professional social media presence. 

The only time I break confidentiality is when you pose a significant and immediate risk to your own or another’s life. In such situations, I may share some information with your GP and/or assigned emergency contact. This I shall do collaboratively, and never behind your back.

Unlike me, you are not bound by confidentiality. You are welcome to share any feedback, concerns and insights regarding my practice and ethics with anyone you want, publicly or online.
